newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ERG sues over funding allegations.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ERG sues over funding allegations.

text.p: Electronics group ERG Ltd said on Tuesday it has started legal action against Victoria's opposition spokesman on transport Peter Batchelor and publisher John Fairfax & Sons Ltd following an article in The Australian Financial Review on Monday.
The Australian Stock Exchange on Monday requested clarification from ERG over the report about funding of its OneLink transport ticketing consortium in Victoria.
ERG said in a statement the article in the Financial Review (AFR) was based on statements made by Batchelor about a report by the Victorian Auditor-General to Victoria's state parliament.

"Those statements and the AFR article misinterpreted the Auditor-General's report, caused a significant drop in ERG's share price and forced the company to request a halt in trading of its shares," ERG said. It described the statements as "ill-considered and misleading".

"As a result of the statements and the AFR article, ERG shareholders, customers, alliance partners and other parties were led to believe that the funding to the project was stopped or at risk," ERG said.
"The company's bankers had, in fact, made a further advance of A$9.9 million only three days prior to the offending statements," it added.
ERG said the proceedings have been brought at Common Law for defamation and will be brought under Section 999 of the Corporations Law.
ERG is the project leader of OneLink. The other project partners are Mayne Nickless Ltd and Fujitsu Australia Ltd, a unit of Fujitsu Ltd 6702.T of Japan.
ERG shares closed 4.0 cents lower at A$1.15 on Tuesday.
